account:
Today appears quiet, with no clear sign of unusual trouble. During my morning market walk, several townsfolk said they had no news; others reported that the baker was carrying wheat at the bakery. My neighbour now says the baker was busy making fresh loaves for today's market. Those accounts fit ordinary bread production, although I did not see the baking myself.

I kept my lunch and town-accounts appointments. The treasury contained 128 emeralds, which I left untouched. The secretary reported no correspondence. There was some confusion about this afternoon's tea: the appointment book named only a neighbour at a dockside cottage, and the secretary's inquiries did not establish the host. I nevertheless found the neighbour at the east-bank cottage and arrived for tea at three. The neighbour welcomed me, described a pleasant afternoon and a visit to the bakery, and reported nothing pressing. This seems to be an ordinary friendly visit, not a meeting about urgent town business.

It is now just after four. I should return to the office for my 16:30 appointment. Tomorrow's schedule includes a ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill and another three o'clock tea here; the neighbour has confirmed that I am welcome for our usual tea.
